articles.title: From robot competitions to inclusive cross‑border AI cooperation
articles.titleCn: 从机器人竞赛到包容性跨境人工智能合作
articles.summary: From robot competitions to inclusive cross‑border AI cooperation
articles.summaryCn: 文章通过RoboCup和世界人形机器人运动会等案例，探讨了具身智能与人形机器人领域跨境合作的机会、技术瓶颈与可行路径，强调开放合作、标准化接口和能力建设对让人工智能创新惠及更多国家的重要性。

paragraphs.en: Robot Lightning sets a new world record at the second World Humanoid Robot Games, held at the National Speed Skating Oval (the Ice Ribbon) in Beijing, China, August 22, 2026. Editor's note: The APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting is set to convene in Shenzhen from November 18–19, 2026. Against growing global interest in {{0}} AI and cross‑border robotics collaboration, CGTN invited Zhou Changjiu, president of RoboCup Asia‑Pacific (RCAP) Confederation and vice‑president of the RoboCup Federation, to share his insights. As co‑founder of the RoboCup Humanoid Soccer League, he draws on decades‑long competition‑driven research experience to analyze opportunities, practical {{2}} and {{3}} pathways for {{1}} cross‑border AI cooperation across the Asia‑Pacific, ahead of the upcoming RCAP Changsha Invitational Tournament in December. The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting will take place in Shenzhen, China, on November 18–19, 2026.
paragraphs.cn: 2026年8月22日，在中国北京国家速滑馆（冰丝带）举行的第二届世界人形机器人运动会上，机器人“闪电”创造了新的世界纪录。编者按：亚太经合组织（APEC）经济领导人会议将于2026年11月18日至19日在深圳召开。在全球对具身人工智能和跨境机器人合作日益关注的背景下，CGTN邀请RoboCup亚太区（RCAP）联合会主席、RoboCup联合会副主席周长久分享他的见解。作为RoboCup人形足球联赛的联合创始人，他凭借数十年以竞赛驱动研究的经验，在即将于12月举行的RCAP长沙邀请赛之前，分析亚太地区包容性跨境人工智能合作的机遇、实际瓶颈和可行路径。亚太经济合作组织（APEC）经济领导人会议将于2026年11月18日至19日在中国深圳举行。

paragraphs.en: As artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes technology and industry worldwide, a key question is how economies can combine their technological {{4}} and industrial strengths so that more people can participate in this innovation and benefit from it. AI is moving beyond the digital {{5}} into the physical world. Embodied AI, particularly humanoid robotics, is advancing from laboratories and competition arenas toward factories and everyday settings. But turning technological {{6}} into practical applications, and individual innovations into international industrial collaboration, remains challenging. Since its first competition in 1997, RoboCup has spent nearly three decades advancing AI and robotics research through international competition.
paragraphs.cn: 随着人工智能（AI）重塑全球技术和产业，一个关键问题是各经济体如何结合各自的技术能力和产业优势，让更多人参与这一创新并从中受益。人工智能正从数字领域走向物理世界。具身人工智能，尤其是人形机器人，正从实验室和竞赛场走向工厂和日常场景。但将技术突破转化为实际应用、将个体创新转化为国际产业合作，仍然充满挑战。自1997年首次举办竞赛以来，RoboCup已用近三十年时间通过国际竞赛推动人工智能和机器人研究。

paragraphs.en:
As one of the co-founders of RoboCup's Humanoid Soccer League, I have been deeply involved in developing its international competition {{7}} and {{8}} cooperation between the global robotics research community and China’s robotics industry. This experience has convinced me that AI's value depends on both technical progress and the cooperation that puts it to use. Combining different countries' technological strengths and industrial resources can enable more developers to innovate and more sectors to benefit. Opportunities: Collaborative innovation from the robotics arena to global value chains
Humanoid robot football offers a useful window into this cooperation. During play, fully {{9}} robots must {{10}} their surroundings, control their movements, make decisions and work together without remote control or human guidance.
paragraphs.cn: 作为RoboCup人形足球联赛的联合创始人之一，我深度参与了其国际竞赛框架的制定，并推动全球机器人研究界与中国机器人产业之间的合作。这一经历让我确信，人工智能的价值既取决于技术进步，也取决于将其付诸应用的合作。结合不同国家的技术优势和产业资源，可以让更多开发者进行创新，让更多行业受益。机遇：从机器人赛场到全球价值链的协同创新。人形机器人足球为这种合作提供了一个有益的窗口。在比赛中，完全自主的机器人必须在没有远程控制或人工引导的情况下感知周围环境、控制自身运动、做出决策并协同工作。

paragraphs.en: Five-a-side and eleven-a-side matches extend the challenge from individual intelligence to multi-robot {{11}} and {{12}} intelligence. In August 2026, a total of 24 international RoboCup teams from 16 countries and regions participated in the RCAP Beijing Masters, held as part of the second World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing. Using humanoid robot platforms supplied by Chinese companies, the teams tested their AI {{13}} and systems {{14}} capabilities under common competition rules. The significance went far beyond the matches. Chinese companies provided robotic hardware and engineering support, while international research teams contributed AI algorithms, software and systems integration {{15}}.
paragraphs.cn: 五人制和十一人制比赛将挑战从个体智能扩展到多机器人协调和集体智能。2026年8月，来自16个国家和地区的24支国际RoboCup队伍参加了作为第二届世界人形机器人运动会组成部分在北京举行的RCAP北京大师赛。这些队伍使用中国公司提供的人形机器人平台，在共同的竞赛规则下测试了各自的人工智能算法和系统集成能力。其意义远超比赛本身。中国公司提供了机器人硬件和工程支持，而国际研究团队则贡献了人工智能算法、软件和系统集成专业知识。

paragraphs.en: Training, testing and competition helped both sides identify technical bottlenecks, improve hardware-software integration and {{16}} development. RCAP is now extending this model from the competition field to industrial applications. The RoboCup Asia-Pacific (RCAP) Changsha Invitational Tournament 2026, scheduled for December 18–20 in Changsha, Hunan Province, will bring together teams from China, Portugal, Brazil, Thailand, Malaysia and Singapore. The tournament will feature humanoid robots developed by a major Chinese heavy-equipment manufacturer based in the host city, a company whose core businesses include construction and agricultural machinery. The company's expansion into humanoid robotics {{17}} how established manufacturers can draw on engineering expertise, manufacturing capacity and real-world industrial environments to advance embodied AI.
paragraphs.cn: 训练、测试和竞赛帮助双方识别技术瓶颈、改进软硬件集成并加速开发。RCAP目前正将这一模式从竞赛领域扩展到工业应用。定于12月18日至20日在湖南长沙举行的2026年RoboCup亚太区（RCAP）长沙邀请赛将汇聚来自中国、葡萄牙、巴西、泰国、马来西亚和新加坡的队伍。该赛事将使用由总部位于主办城市的一家中国大型重型装备制造商开发的人形机器人，该公司核心业务包括建筑和农业机械。该公司向人形机器人领域的拓展表明，成熟的制造商可以借助工程专业知识、制造能力和真实工业环境来推进具身人工智能。

paragraphs.en: Participants will use these robots for training, joint research and international competition, while exploring potential applications in industrial production and household services. The event aims to connect China's robot platforms and application environments with the global RoboCup developer community and leading industrial enterprises. By bringing competition, collaborative research and real-world testing together, it seeks to create a clearer pathway from technical experimentation to practical application. Industrial testing can also generate valuable operational data. Repeated trials can reveal how variations in lighting, object placement or workflow affect robot performance, helping researchers identify weaknesses and {{18}} their systems.
paragraphs.cn: 参赛者将使用这些机器人进行训练、联合研究和国际竞赛，同时探索在工业生产和家庭服务中的潜在应用。该活动旨在将中国的机器人平台和应用环境与全球RoboCup开发者社区及领先工业企业连接起来。通过将竞赛、合作研究和真实环境测试相结合，它力求开辟一条从技术实验到实际应用的更清晰路径。工业测试还能产生有价值的运行数据。反复试验可以揭示光照、物体摆放或工作流程的变化如何影响机器人性能，帮助研究人员发现弱点并改进系统。

paragraphs.en: For these benefits to extend across borders, partners need clear agreements on data access and reuse, supported by {{19}} for security, privacy and {{20}} property. These arrangements can help turn access to industrial environments into shared opportunities for research and innovation. China's extensive robotics manufacturing {{21}}, efficient supply chains, rapid engineering {{22}} and varied applications in smart manufacturing and services offer international researchers valuable opportunities for development and {{23}}. In return, Chinese manufacturers can use the diverse AI algorithms, software solutions and technical feedback of global developers to improve their products and software ecosystems. This two-way exchange demonstrates how hardware, software, AI algorithms and application scenarios can {{24}} one another across global robotics value chains, creating more opportunities for shared innovation.
paragraphs.cn: 要让这些益处跨越国界，合作伙伴需要在数据访问和再利用方面达成明确协议，并辅以安全、隐私和知识产权保障。这些安排有助于将对工业环境的访问转化为研究和创新的共同机遇。中国庞大的机器人制造生态系统、高效的供应链、快速的工程迭代以及智能制造和服务领域的多样化应用，为国际研究人员提供了宝贵的发展和验证机会。反过来，中国制造商可以利用全球开发者多样的人工智能算法、软件解决方案和技术反馈来改进其产品和软件生态系统。这种双向交流表明，硬件、软件、人工智能算法和应用场景可以在全球机器人价值链上相互补充，创造更多共同创新的机会。

paragraphs.en:
Barriers: Technical capability alone does not guarantee real-world use
Despite rapid advances in AI and robotics, moving a technology from the laboratory into everyday use remains difficult. The {{25}} often lie not in the intelligence of the robot itself, but in {{26}}, device interfaces, technical standards and system {{27}}. Consider a simple task: how does a service robot take an elevator? Many robots can already navigate autonomously, recognize their surroundings and avoid obstacles. Yet in some commercial buildings in Singapore and elsewhere, elevator control systems offer no usable communication interface for third-party robots.
paragraphs.cn: 障碍：仅靠技术能力并不能保证实际应用。尽管人工智能和机器人技术飞速发展，但将技术从实验室推向日常使用仍然困难重重。障碍往往不在于机器人本身的智能，而在于基础设施、设备接口、技术标准和系统兼容性。考虑一个简单的任务：服务机器人如何乘坐电梯？许多机器人已经能够自主导航、识别周围环境并避开障碍物。然而在新加坡及其他地方的一些商业建筑中，电梯控制系统没有为第三方机器人提供可用的通信接口。

paragraphs.en: A robot may be unable to call an elevator or select a floor digitally, and may instead require an add-on mechanical arm to physically press the buttons. The contrast is striking: a robot capable of sophisticated autonomous decisions can still be held back by something as basic as an elevator interface. Of course, elevators are safety-critical systems. Access to their controls must meet requirements for physical safety, cybersecurity and building management. Safe integration requires standardized interfaces, appropriate {{28}} and clear access rules.
paragraphs.cn: 机器人可能无法以数字方式呼叫电梯或选择楼层，反而可能需要附加机械臂来物理按下按钮。对比鲜明：一个能够做出复杂自主决策的机器人，仍可能被电梯接口这样基本的问题所阻碍。当然，电梯是安全关键系统。对其控制系统的访问必须满足物理安全、网络安全和建筑管理的要求。安全集成需要标准化接口、适当的认证和明确的访问规则。

paragraphs.en: Singapore's national standard for data exchange between robots, elevators and automated doors is a step in this direction, though upgrading existing buildings takes time. Similar problems arise in industrial automation. Robots from different manufacturers often use different communication protocols, software architectures and control systems. An AI algorithm that performs well on one platform may need substantial software adaptation, parameter tuning and testing before it can run on another. Differences in development tools, operating environments, data-use requirements and intellectual property arrangements can further complicate international joint research and the reuse of research results.
paragraphs.cn: 新加坡关于机器人、电梯和自动门之间数据交换的国家标准是朝这一方向迈出的一步，不过升级现有建筑需要时间。工业自动化中也存在类似问题。不同制造商的机器人往往使用不同的通信协议、软件架构和控制系统。在一个平台上表现良好的人工智能算法，在另一个平台上运行之前可能需要大量的软件适配、参数调整和测试。开发工具、运行环境、数据使用要求和知识产权安排方面的差异，可能进一步使国际联合研究和研究成果的再利用复杂化。

paragraphs.en: Technical compatibility is only part of the challenge. A robot that performs well in a trial may still require further assessment or approval before deployment in another economy. Differences in certification requirements, procurement procedures and market access can add time and cost to joint projects. Cooperation therefore needs more than compatible hardware and software. It also depends on transparent requirements and coordination among technology providers, regulators and users.
paragraphs.cn: 技术兼容性只是挑战的一部分。在试验中表现良好的机器人，在另一个经济体部署之前仍可能需要进一步评估或审批。认证要求、采购程序和市场准入方面的差异会增加联合项目的时间和成本。因此，合作需要的不仅仅是兼容的硬件和软件。它还取决于透明的要求以及技术提供者、监管者和用户之间的协调。

paragraphs.en:
These examples point to a broader lesson: technological sophistication does not automatically translate into practical usability, let alone into benefits that are widely shared. A breakthrough in one component does not establish the maturity of an entire system, and success in a laboratory does not guarantee reliable performance in the real world. Wider adoption therefore depends not only on stronger AI algorithms, but also on interoperability, standardized interfaces, system safety and dependable performance in real operating environments. Pathways: Making the fruits of AI innovation more accessible worldwide through open cooperation
How can international collaboration lower development barriers and help more countries, companies and researchers participate in AI innovation? RoboCup's nearly three decades of experience offer practical lessons.
paragraphs.cn: 这些例子指向一个更广泛的教训：技术先进性并不会自动转化为实际可用性，更不用说转化为广泛共享的益处。一个组件的突破并不能确立整个系统的成熟度，实验室中的成功也不能保证在现实世界中的可靠性能。因此，更广泛的采用不仅取决于更强的人工智能算法，还取决于互操作性、标准化接口、系统安全以及在真实运行环境中的可靠性能。路径：通过开放合作让人工智能创新成果更易惠及全球。国际合作如何降低发展壁垒，帮助更多国家、公司和研究人员参与人工智能创新？RoboCup近三十年的经验提供了实际借鉴。

paragraphs.en: Even when teams from different countries work on the same task and use identical hardware, they often choose very different technical approaches. Some specialize in motion control, others in computer vision and autonomous decision-making, and still others in software architecture or multi-robot coordination. Common rules, shared testing environments and technical exchanges let teams compare, validate and improve these approaches. At international competitions, I have often witnessed teams compete fiercely on the field and then, after the final whistle, exchange AI algorithms, share experience and sometimes begin long-term research partnerships. Shared technical goals leave room for different development paths.
paragraphs.cn: 即使来自不同国家的团队从事同一任务并使用相同的硬件，他们也常常选择截然不同的技术路径。有的专攻运动控制，有的专攻计算机视觉和自主决策，还有的专攻软件架构或多机器人协调。共同的规则、共享的测试环境和技术交流让团队能够比较、验证和改进这些方法。在国际比赛中，我经常看到各队在赛场上激烈竞争，而在终场哨响后交换人工智能算法、分享经验，有时还开启长期研究合作。共同的技术目标为不同的发展路径留出了空间。

paragraphs.en: This approach is consistent with APEC's principles of voluntary cooperation and consensus. Economies should be able to exchange experience and choose technologies suited to their own needs, resources and stages of development, rather than follow a single prescribed model. Joint research and talent exchanges can support those choices, building capabilities through sustained testing and adaptation. Three practical priorities follow. First, build open and interoperable development platforms.
paragraphs.cn: 这种做法与APEC自愿合作和协商一致的原则相一致。各经济体应当能够交流经验，并根据自身需求、资源和发展阶段选择适合自己的技术，而不是遵循单一规定模式。联合研究和人才交流可以支持这些选择，通过持续测试和调整来建设能力。由此得出三个实际优先事项。第一，构建开放且可互操作的开发平台。

paragraphs.en: Accessible software development kits, simulation tools, standardized interfaces and technical documentation can reduce integration costs and encourage the reuse of algorithms and software modules. This allows developers to spend less time on repetitive integration work and more on core technical problems. Second, make real-world applications the focus of joint R&D. Universities, research institutes and companies from different countries can work on common platforms to develop and validate solutions for smart manufacturing, logistics, public services and home assistance. China's robotics supply chains and application scenarios can complement the AI algorithms and software expertise of developers worldwide, accelerating the transition from research to deployment.
paragraphs.cn: 易于获取的软件开发工具包、仿真工具、标准化接口和技术文档可以降低集成成本，鼓励算法和软件模块的再利用。这使开发者能够减少在重复性集成工作上花费的时间，将更多精力投入核心技术问题。第二，将实际应用作为联合研发的重点。来自不同国家的大学、研究机构和公司可以在共同平台上合作，开发和验证智能制造、物流、公共服务和家庭辅助的解决方案。中国的机器人供应链和应用场景可以补充全球开发者的人工智能算法和软件专长，加速从研究到部署的转化。

paragraphs.en: Third, strengthen research partnerships and talent exchanges across the Asia-Pacific. Joint laboratories could pair university teams with industrial partners to test robots on shared tasks, while researcher exchanges could provide practical training in deployment and maintenance. Participants could take tested methods and engineering experience back to their institutions and adapt them to local needs. International competitions can help initiate these relationships and keep partners working toward shared technical goals. Wider access to advanced products matters.
paragraphs.cn: 第三，加强亚太地区的研究伙伴关系和人才交流。联合实验室可以将大学团队与产业伙伴配对，在共同任务上测试机器人，而研究人员交流可以提供部署和维护方面的实践培训。参与者可以将经过测试的方法和工程经验带回各自机构，并根据当地需求进行调整。国际竞赛可以帮助建立这些关系，并推动合作伙伴朝着共同的技术目标努力。更广泛地获取先进产品很重要。

paragraphs.en:
So does the capacity to develop and adapt the technology behind them. Lowering barriers to innovation enables research teams in different countries to contribute according to their strengths and build lasting research and application capabilities. Such capacity-building is a gradual, long-term process, not a one-off transfer. Innovation to deployment: Leveraging China's strengths for shared global innovation
China's growing strengths in robotics manufacturing, supply-chain efficiency and real-world applications are creating new opportunities for AI developers around the world. At the same time, the AI algorithms, software and application expertise of international teams are helping Chinese robotics companies improve their technologies.
paragraphs.cn: 开发和适配这些产品背后技术的能力同样重要。降低创新壁垒使不同国家的研究团队能够根据自身优势做出贡献，并建立持久的研究和应用能力。这种能力建设是一个渐进的长期过程，而不是一次性转移。从创新到部署：发挥中国优势，促进全球共同创新。中国在机器人制造、供应链效率和实际应用方面日益增强的实力，正在为世界各地的AI开发者创造新机遇。与此同时，国际团队的AI算法、软件和应用专长也在帮助中国机器人企业改进技术。

paragraphs.en: Moving from innovation to large-scale deployment still requires sustained engineering work, open collaboration and talent development. RoboCup's experience shows that competition and cooperation can reinforce each other: shared challenges encourage diverse solutions, while open exchange helps knowledge and technology advance faster. Connecting China's robotics industry and real-world application environments with the creativity of developers worldwide can lower barriers to innovation, enabling more people to contribute to and benefit from advances in robotics and AI. The long-term promise of international AI cooperation lies in translating innovation in the competition arena into practical solutions for factories, services and everyday life, delivering tangible benefits across industries and societies.
paragraphs.cn: 从创新走向大规模部署仍然需要持续的工程工作、开放合作和人才培养。RoboCup的经验表明，竞争与合作可以相互促进：共同的挑战鼓励多样化的解决方案，而开放交流有助于知识和技术更快进步。将中国机器人产业和真实应用环境与全球开发者的创造力连接起来，可以降低创新壁垒，让更多人能够为机器人和人工智能的进步做出贡献并从中受益。国际人工智能合作的长期前景在于将竞赛场上的创新转化为工厂、服务和日常生活的实际解决方案，为各行业和社会带来切实利益。

But turning technological breakthroughs into practical applications, and individual innovations into international industrial collaboration, remains challenging.
Since its first competition in 1997, RoboCup has spent nearly three decades advancing AI and robotics research through international competition.
As one of the co-founders of RoboCup's Humanoid Soccer League, I have been deeply involved in developing its international competition framework and fostering cooperation between the global robotics research community and China’s robotics industry.
This experience has convinced me that AI's value depends on both technical progress and the cooperation that puts it to use. Combining different countries' technological strengths and industrial resources can enable more developers to innovate and more sectors to benefit.
Opportunities: Collaborative innovation from the robotics arena to global value chains
Humanoid robot football offers a useful window into this cooperation.
During play, fully autonomous robots must perceive their surroundings, control their movements, make decisions and work together without remote control or human guidance.
Five-a-side and eleven-a-side matches extend the challenge from individual intelligence to multi-robot coordination and collective intelligence.
In August 2026, a total of 24 international RoboCup teams from 16 countries and regions participated in the RCAP Beijing Masters, held as part of the second World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing.
Using humanoid robot platforms supplied by Chinese companies, the teams tested their AI algorithms and systems integration capabilities under common competition rules.
The significance went far beyond the matches. Chinese companies provided robotic hardware and engineering support, while international research teams contributed AI algorithms, software and systems integration expertise.
Training, testing and competition helped both sides identify technical bottlenecks, improve hardware-software integration and accelerate development.
RCAP is now extending this model from the competition field to industrial applications. The RoboCup Asia-Pacific (RCAP) Changsha Invitational Tournament 2026, scheduled for December 18–20 in Changsha, Hunan Province, will bring together teams from China, Portugal, Brazil, Thailand, Malaysia and Singapore.
The tournament will feature humanoid robots developed by a major Chinese heavy-equipment manufacturer based in the host city, a company whose core businesses include construction and agricultural machinery.
The company's expansion into humanoid robotics illustrates how established manufacturers can draw on engineering expertise, manufacturing capacity and real-world industrial environments to advance embodied AI.
Participants will use these robots for training, joint research and international competition, while exploring potential applications in industrial production and household services.
The event aims to connect China's robot platforms and application environments with the global RoboCup developer community and leading industrial enterprises.
By bringing competition, collaborative research and real-world testing together, it seeks to create a clearer pathway from technical experimentation to practical application.
Industrial testing can also generate valuable operational data. Repeated trials can reveal how variations in lighting, object placement or workflow affect robot performance, helping researchers identify weaknesses and refine their systems.
For these benefits to extend across borders, partners need clear agreements on data access and reuse, supported by safeguards for security, privacy and intellectual property.
These arrangements can help turn access to industrial environments into shared opportunities for research and innovation.
China's extensive robotics manufacturing ecosystem, efficient supply chains, rapid engineering iteration and varied applications in smart manufacturing and services offer international researchers valuable opportunities for development and validation.
In return, Chinese manufacturers can use the diverse AI algorithms, software solutions and technical feedback of global developers to improve their products and software ecosystems.
This two-way exchange demonstrates how hardware, software, AI algorithms and application scenarios can complement one another across global robotics value chains, creating more opportunities for shared innovation.
Barriers: Technical capability alone does not guarantee real-world use
Despite rapid advances in AI and robotics, moving a technology from the laboratory into everyday use remains difficult.
The obstacles often lie not in the intelligence of the robot itself, but in infrastructure, device interfaces, technical standards and system compatibility.
Consider a simple task: how does a service robot take an elevator?
Many robots can already navigate autonomously, recognize their surroundings and avoid obstacles. Yet in some commercial buildings in Singapore and elsewhere, elevator control systems offer no usable communication interface for third-party robots.
A robot may be unable to call an elevator or select a floor digitally, and may instead require an add-on mechanical arm to physically press the buttons.
The contrast is striking: a robot capable of sophisticated autonomous decisions can still be held back by something as basic as an elevator interface.
Of course, elevators are safety-critical systems. Access to their controls must meet requirements for physical safety, cybersecurity and building management.
Safe integration requires standardized interfaces, appropriate certification and clear access rules.
Singapore's national standard for data exchange between robots, elevators and automated doors is a step in this direction, though upgrading existing buildings takes time.
Similar problems arise in industrial automation. Robots from different manufacturers often use different communication protocols, software architectures and control systems.
An AI algorithm that performs well on one platform may need substantial software adaptation, parameter tuning and testing before it can run on another.
Differences in development tools, operating environments, data-use requirements and intellectual property arrangements can further complicate international joint research and the reuse of research results.
Technical compatibility is only part of the challenge. A robot that performs well in a trial may still require further assessment or approval before deployment in another economy.
Differences in certification requirements, procurement procedures and market access can add time and cost to joint projects. Cooperation therefore needs more than compatible hardware and software.
It also depends on transparent requirements and coordination among technology providers, regulators and users.
These examples point to a broader lesson: technological sophistication does not automatically translate into practical usability, let alone into benefits that are widely shared.
A breakthrough in one component does not establish the maturity of an entire system, and success in a laboratory does not guarantee reliable performance in the real world.
Wider adoption therefore depends not only on stronger AI algorithms, but also on interoperability, standardized interfaces, system safety and dependable performance in real operating environments.
Pathways: Making the fruits of AI innovation more accessible worldwide through open cooperation
How can international collaboration lower development barriers and help more countries, companies and researchers participate in AI innovation? RoboCup's nearly three decades of experience offer practical lessons.
Even when teams from different countries work on the same task and use identical hardware, they often choose very different technical approaches.
Some specialize in motion control, others in computer vision and autonomous decision-making, and still others in software architecture or multi-robot coordination.
Common rules, shared testing environments and technical exchanges let teams compare, validate and improve these approaches.
At international competitions, I have often witnessed teams compete fiercely on the field and then, after the final whistle, exchange AI algorithms, share experience and sometimes begin long-term research partnerships.
Shared technical goals leave room for different development paths. This approach is consistent with APEC's principles of voluntary cooperation and consensus.
Economies should be able to exchange experience and choose technologies suited to their own needs, resources and stages of development, rather than follow a single prescribed model.
Joint research and talent exchanges can support those choices, building capabilities through sustained testing and adaptation.
Three practical priorities follow.
First, build open and interoperable development platforms. Accessible software development kits, simulation tools, standardized interfaces and technical documentation can reduce integration costs and encourage the reuse of algorithms and software modules.
This allows developers to spend less time on repetitive integration work and more on core technical problems.
Second, make real-world applications the focus of joint R&D. Universities, research institutes and companies from different countries can work on common platforms to develop and validate solutions for smart manufacturing, logistics, public services and home assistance.
China's robotics supply chains and application scenarios can complement the AI algorithms and software expertise of developers worldwide, accelerating the transition from research to deployment.
Third, strengthen research partnerships and talent exchanges across the Asia-Pacific. Joint laboratories could pair university teams with industrial partners to test robots on shared tasks, while researcher exchanges could provide practical training in deployment and maintenance.
Participants could take tested methods and engineering experience back to their institutions and adapt them to local needs. International competitions can help initiate these relationships and keep partners working toward shared technical goals.
Wider access to advanced products matters. So does the capacity to develop and adapt the technology behind them.
Lowering barriers to innovation enables research teams in different countries to contribute according to their strengths and build lasting research and application capabilities.
Such capacity-building is a gradual, long-term process, not a one-off transfer.
Innovation to deployment: Leveraging China's strengths for shared global innovation
China's growing strengths in robotics manufacturing, supply-chain efficiency and real-world applications are creating new opportunities for AI developers around the world.
At the same time, the AI algorithms, software and application expertise of international teams are helping Chinese robotics companies improve their technologies.
Moving from innovation to large-scale deployment still requires sustained engineering work, open collaboration and talent development.
RoboCup's experience shows that competition and cooperation can reinforce each other: shared challenges encourage diverse solutions, while open exchange helps knowledge and technology advance faster.
Connecting China's robotics industry and real-world application environments with the creativity of developers worldwide can lower barriers to innovation, enabling more people to contribute to and benefit from advances in robotics and AI.
The long-term promise of international AI cooperation lies in translating innovation in the competition arena into practical solutions for factories, services and everyday life, delivering tangible benefits across industries and societies.

2026年8月22日，在中国北京国家速滑馆（冰丝带）举行的第二届世界人形机器人运动会上，机器人“闪电”创造了新的世界纪录。编者按：亚太经合组织（APEC）经济领导人会议将于2026年11月18日至19日在深圳召开。在全球对具身人工智能和跨境机器人合作日益关注的背景下，CGTN邀请RoboCup亚太区（RCAP）联合会主席、RoboCup联合会副主席周长久分享他的见解。作为RoboCup人形足球联赛的联合创始人，他凭借数十年以竞赛驱动研究的经验，在即将于12月举行的RCAP长沙邀请赛之前，分析亚太地区包容性跨境人工智能合作的机遇、实际瓶颈和可行路径。亚太经济合作组织（APEC）经济领导人会议将于2026年11月18日至19日在中国深圳举行。

随着人工智能（AI）重塑全球技术和产业，一个关键问题是各经济体如何结合各自的技术能力和产业优势，让更多人参与这一创新并从中受益。人工智能正从数字领域走向物理世界。具身人工智能，尤其是人形机器人，正从实验室和竞赛场走向工厂和日常场景。但将技术突破转化为实际应用、将个体创新转化为国际产业合作，仍然充满挑战。自1997年首次举办竞赛以来，RoboCup已用近三十年时间通过国际竞赛推动人工智能和机器人研究。

作为RoboCup人形足球联赛的联合创始人之一，我深度参与了其国际竞赛框架的制定，并推动全球机器人研究界与中国机器人产业之间的合作。这一经历让我确信，人工智能的价值既取决于技术进步，也取决于将其付诸应用的合作。结合不同国家的技术优势和产业资源，可以让更多开发者进行创新，让更多行业受益。机遇：从机器人赛场到全球价值链的协同创新。人形机器人足球为这种合作提供了一个有益的窗口。在比赛中，完全自主的机器人必须在没有远程控制或人工引导的情况下感知周围环境、控制自身运动、做出决策并协同工作。

五人制和十一人制比赛将挑战从个体智能扩展到多机器人协调和集体智能。2026年8月，来自16个国家和地区的24支国际RoboCup队伍参加了作为第二届世界人形机器人运动会组成部分在北京举行的RCAP北京大师赛。这些队伍使用中国公司提供的人形机器人平台，在共同的竞赛规则下测试了各自的人工智能算法和系统集成能力。其意义远超比赛本身。中国公司提供了机器人硬件和工程支持，而国际研究团队则贡献了人工智能算法、软件和系统集成专业知识。

训练、测试和竞赛帮助双方识别技术瓶颈、改进软硬件集成并加速开发。RCAP目前正将这一模式从竞赛领域扩展到工业应用。定于12月18日至20日在湖南长沙举行的2026年RoboCup亚太区（RCAP）长沙邀请赛将汇聚来自中国、葡萄牙、巴西、泰国、马来西亚和新加坡的队伍。该赛事将使用由总部位于主办城市的一家中国大型重型装备制造商开发的人形机器人，该公司核心业务包括建筑和农业机械。该公司向人形机器人领域的拓展表明，成熟的制造商可以借助工程专业知识、制造能力和真实工业环境来推进具身人工智能。

参赛者将使用这些机器人进行训练、联合研究和国际竞赛，同时探索在工业生产和家庭服务中的潜在应用。该活动旨在将中国的机器人平台和应用环境与全球RoboCup开发者社区及领先工业企业连接起来。通过将竞赛、合作研究和真实环境测试相结合，它力求开辟一条从技术实验到实际应用的更清晰路径。工业测试还能产生有价值的运行数据。反复试验可以揭示光照、物体摆放或工作流程的变化如何影响机器人性能，帮助研究人员发现弱点并改进系统。

要让这些益处跨越国界，合作伙伴需要在数据访问和再利用方面达成明确协议，并辅以安全、隐私和知识产权保障。这些安排有助于将对工业环境的访问转化为研究和创新的共同机遇。中国庞大的机器人制造生态系统、高效的供应链、快速的工程迭代以及智能制造和服务领域的多样化应用，为国际研究人员提供了宝贵的发展和验证机会。反过来，中国制造商可以利用全球开发者多样的人工智能算法、软件解决方案和技术反馈来改进其产品和软件生态系统。这种双向交流表明，硬件、软件、人工智能算法和应用场景可以在全球机器人价值链上相互补充，创造更多共同创新的机会。

障碍：仅靠技术能力并不能保证实际应用。尽管人工智能和机器人技术飞速发展，但将技术从实验室推向日常使用仍然困难重重。障碍往往不在于机器人本身的智能，而在于基础设施、设备接口、技术标准和系统兼容性。考虑一个简单的任务：服务机器人如何乘坐电梯？许多机器人已经能够自主导航、识别周围环境并避开障碍物。然而在新加坡及其他地方的一些商业建筑中，电梯控制系统没有为第三方机器人提供可用的通信接口。

机器人可能无法以数字方式呼叫电梯或选择楼层，反而可能需要附加机械臂来物理按下按钮。对比鲜明：一个能够做出复杂自主决策的机器人，仍可能被电梯接口这样基本的问题所阻碍。当然，电梯是安全关键系统。对其控制系统的访问必须满足物理安全、网络安全和建筑管理的要求。安全集成需要标准化接口、适当的认证和明确的访问规则。

新加坡关于机器人、电梯和自动门之间数据交换的国家标准是朝这一方向迈出的一步，不过升级现有建筑需要时间。工业自动化中也存在类似问题。不同制造商的机器人往往使用不同的通信协议、软件架构和控制系统。在一个平台上表现良好的人工智能算法，在另一个平台上运行之前可能需要大量的软件适配、参数调整和测试。开发工具、运行环境、数据使用要求和知识产权安排方面的差异，可能进一步使国际联合研究和研究成果的再利用复杂化。

技术兼容性只是挑战的一部分。在试验中表现良好的机器人，在另一个经济体部署之前仍可能需要进一步评估或审批。认证要求、采购程序和市场准入方面的差异会增加联合项目的时间和成本。因此，合作需要的不仅仅是兼容的硬件和软件。它还取决于透明的要求以及技术提供者、监管者和用户之间的协调。

这些例子指向一个更广泛的教训：技术先进性并不会自动转化为实际可用性，更不用说转化为广泛共享的益处。一个组件的突破并不能确立整个系统的成熟度，实验室中的成功也不能保证在现实世界中的可靠性能。因此，更广泛的采用不仅取决于更强的人工智能算法，还取决于互操作性、标准化接口、系统安全以及在真实运行环境中的可靠性能。路径：通过开放合作让人工智能创新成果更易惠及全球。国际合作如何降低发展壁垒，帮助更多国家、公司和研究人员参与人工智能创新？RoboCup近三十年的经验提供了实际借鉴。

即使来自不同国家的团队从事同一任务并使用相同的硬件，他们也常常选择截然不同的技术路径。有的专攻运动控制，有的专攻计算机视觉和自主决策，还有的专攻软件架构或多机器人协调。共同的规则、共享的测试环境和技术交流让团队能够比较、验证和改进这些方法。在国际比赛中，我经常看到各队在赛场上激烈竞争，而在终场哨响后交换人工智能算法、分享经验，有时还开启长期研究合作。共同的技术目标为不同的发展路径留出了空间。

这种做法与APEC自愿合作和协商一致的原则相一致。各经济体应当能够交流经验，并根据自身需求、资源和发展阶段选择适合自己的技术，而不是遵循单一规定模式。联合研究和人才交流可以支持这些选择，通过持续测试和调整来建设能力。由此得出三个实际优先事项。第一，构建开放且可互操作的开发平台。

易于获取的软件开发工具包、仿真工具、标准化接口和技术文档可以降低集成成本，鼓励算法和软件模块的再利用。这使开发者能够减少在重复性集成工作上花费的时间，将更多精力投入核心技术问题。第二，将实际应用作为联合研发的重点。来自不同国家的大学、研究机构和公司可以在共同平台上合作，开发和验证智能制造、物流、公共服务和家庭辅助的解决方案。中国的机器人供应链和应用场景可以补充全球开发者的人工智能算法和软件专长，加速从研究到部署的转化。

第三，加强亚太地区的研究伙伴关系和人才交流。联合实验室可以将大学团队与产业伙伴配对，在共同任务上测试机器人，而研究人员交流可以提供部署和维护方面的实践培训。参与者可以将经过测试的方法和工程经验带回各自机构，并根据当地需求进行调整。国际竞赛可以帮助建立这些关系，并推动合作伙伴朝着共同的技术目标努力。更广泛地获取先进产品很重要。

开发和适配这些产品背后技术的能力同样重要。降低创新壁垒使不同国家的研究团队能够根据自身优势做出贡献，并建立持久的研究和应用能力。这种能力建设是一个渐进的长期过程，而不是一次性转移。从创新到部署：发挥中国优势，促进全球共同创新。中国在机器人制造、供应链效率和实际应用方面日益增强的实力，正在为世界各地的AI开发者创造新机遇。与此同时，国际团队的AI算法、软件和应用专长也在帮助中国机器人企业改进技术。

从创新走向大规模部署仍然需要持续的工程工作、开放合作和人才培养。RoboCup的经验表明，竞争与合作可以相互促进：共同的挑战鼓励多样化的解决方案，而开放交流有助于知识和技术更快进步。将中国机器人产业和真实应用环境与全球开发者的创造力连接起来，可以降低创新壁垒，让更多人能够为机器人和人工智能的进步做出贡献并从中受益。国际人工智能合作的长期前景在于将竞赛场上的创新转化为工厂、服务和日常生活的实际解决方案，为各行业和社会带来切实利益。

articles.title: From resources to manufacturing: A new model of Asia-Pacific growth
articles.titleCn: 从资源到制造：亚太增长的新模式
articles.summary: From resources to manufacturing: A new model of Asia-Pacific growth
articles.summaryCn: 亚太地区经济体正通过整合资源、投资、技术和市场，构建更一体化的工业网络，从简单的原材料交换转向跨境的产业链合作，为区域增长创造共享机遇。

paragraphs.en: The supply chain behind an electric vehicle sold in Southeast Asia can stretch across continents: nickel from Indonesia, lithium from Chile, investment and manufacturing {{1}} from across Asia and a growing regional market bringing these elements together. It is a reminder that the economic value of a product increasingly lies not in any single country's resources or factories, but in the connections between them. Across the Asia-Pacific, economies are drawing on their respective strengths to build more {{0}} industrial networks, moving beyond the simple exchange of raw materials and finished goods. From mineral {{2}} to vehicle manufacturing and battery supply, these links are creating {{25}} for investment, technology transfer and industrial development across the region. Indonesia offers a {{3}} example of how a resource-rich economy can seek a greater role in global industry.
paragraphs.cn: 在东南亚销售的一辆电动汽车背后的供应链可以跨越多个大洲：来自印度尼西亚的镍、来自智利的锂、来自亚洲各地的投资和制造专长，以及一个将这些要素汇聚在一起的不断增长的区域市场。这提醒人们，一个产品的经济价值越来越不在于任何单一国家的资源或工厂，而在于它们之间的联系。在整个亚太地区，各经济体正利用各自的优势构建更加一体化的工业网络，超越简单的原材料和成品交换。从矿物加工到汽车制造和电池供应，这些联系正在为整个地区的投资、技术转让和工业发展创造机会。印度尼西亚提供了一个引人注目的例子，说明一个资源丰富的经济体如何寻求在全球工业中发挥更大的作用。

paragraphs.en: As the world's leading nickel producer, Indonesia saw its mined nickel output increase by an estimated 13% in 2025, according to the US Geological Survey. The country has attracted investment in {{17}} {{4}} and processing, seeking to turn its mineral resources into higher-value products rather than relying on raw ore exports. A worker inspects plants at a tree nursery facility inside a nickel mining site operated by PT Vale Indonesia in Sorowako, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, February 4, 2026. The supply chain behind an electric vehicle sold in Southeast Asia can stretch across continents: nickel from Indonesia, lithium from Chile, investment and manufacturing expertise from across Asia and a growing regional market bringing these elements together. It is a reminder that the economic value of a product increasingly lies not in any single country's resources or factories, but in the connections between them.
Across the Asia-Pacific, economies are drawing on their respective strengths to build more integrated industrial networks, moving beyond the simple exchange of raw materials and finished goods. From mineral processing to vehicle manufacturing and battery supply, these links are creating opportunities for investment, technology transfer and industrial development across the region.
Indonesia offers a striking example of how a resource-rich economy can seek a greater role in global industry. As the world's leading nickel producer, Indonesia saw its mined nickel output increase by an estimated 13% in 2025, according to the US Geological Survey. The country has attracted investment in domestic smelting and processing, seeking to turn its mineral resources into higher-value products rather than relying on raw ore exports.
A worker inspects plants at a tree nursery facility inside a nickel mining site operated by PT Vale Indonesia in Sorowako, South Sulawesi, Indonesia, February 4, 2026. 
Nickel is widely used in stainless steel and is also an important material in some electric vehicle batteries. By expanding its processing capacity, Indonesia is positioning itself to participate in a broader industrial chain that connects mineral extraction with battery production and vehicle manufacturing. Its resources can complement the technological expertise, investment and manufacturing capabilities available elsewhere in Asia.
That cooperation is unfolding alongside the rapid expansion of Southeast Asia's electric vehicle market. Sales of electric cars in the region more than doubled in 2025 to exceed half a million, with such vehicles accounting for nearly one in five new cars sold, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). Vietnam, Indonesia and Thailand were among the markets leading the growth.
The expanding market is attracting automakers and suppliers to the region, creating opportunities to develop local production and connect manufacturers with regional supply networks. Chinese carmakers have become an increasingly important part of this development. More than half of the electric cars sold in Southeast Asia in 2025 were Chinese brands, while manufacturers have also been expanding production facilities in the region, the IEA said.
A production workshop for new energy vehicles in Zhengzhou, China, September 30, 2026. 
This creates a broader economic relationship: Indonesia's mineral resources can support battery-related industries, while Southeast Asia's growing consumer markets and manufacturing base provide opportunities for investment and production. The benefits can extend beyond vehicle makers to suppliers, workers and businesses involved in components and related services.
Further across the Pacific, Chile is seeking to turn its mineral wealth into a stronger domestic industry. A major producer of copper and lithium, the South American economy supplies materials essential to electrification, from power grids and electric motors to rechargeable batteries. Asia received 95% of Chile's lithium exports in 2025, with China accounting for 67%, according to the country's Subsecretariat of International Economic Relations.
But Chile's ambition extends beyond supplying overseas manufacturers. Its National Lithium Strategy aims to attract capital and technology, expand production and promote the development of downstream industries. A partnership between state-owned copper producer Codelco and lithium company SQM is a key part of that effort, combining public-sector participation with private-sector expertise to develop lithium resources.
Aerial view of brine ponds and processing areas at the lithium mine operated by Chilean company SQM (Sociedad Quimica Minera) in the Atacama Desert, Calama, Chile, September 12, 2022. 
Canada is also working to build a more complete domestic supply chain, connecting its mineral resources with processing and advanced manufacturing. As of March 2025, the country had 31 critical mineral processing facilities and 171 advanced projects, including 28 processing projects, according to the Canadian government. Its NextStar Energy battery plant in Ontario, backed by an investment of 5 billion Canadian dollars ($3.54 billion), began producing electric vehicle battery modules in 2024 and battery cells for energy storage systems in November 2025. The project reflects a broader effort to turn Canada's mineral resources into a foundation for advanced manufacturing.
From Indonesia's nickel processing and Southeast Asia's expanding vehicle industry to Chile's mineral exports, these connections show how economies can turn their individual advantages into shared opportunities. When resources, investment, technology and markets reinforce one another, cooperation can create value across borders and give more economies a stake in the growth of the Asia-Pacific.

Across the Asia-Pacific, frequent extreme weather, uneven public service capacity and rising energy demand driven by growing computing needs present common challenges for many APEC economies.
CGTN spoke with two experts in quantum computing and next-generation computing: Professor Lin Jing from City University of Hong Kong and Professor Wen Yonggang, associate provost at Nanyang Technological University and a fellow of the Singapore Academy of Engineering.
AI-powered meteorological early warning systems process real-time weather data to issue typhoon and flood alerts and support local disaster preparedness.
Open-source AI tools for public health are shared regionally to assist local medical teams in providing routine care.
Embodied intelligence prototypes showcased at humanoid robot competitions are seen as promising tools for elderly care and on-site emergency rescue, helping to fill service gaps where labor is scarce.
Professor Lin Jing from City University of Hong Kong. 
Professor Lin Jing, academic curator of the "Future Computing · Future Compute Power" forum at the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference, said quantum-AI hybrid architectures offer unique research advantages for high-fidelity climate simulation and molecular-level drug development, yet the technology remains largely confined to laboratory research.
"Quantum computing is still in its foundational research phase. It is not yet ready for widespread deployment as standard digital infrastructure. While it offers theoretical advantages for modelling complex natural systems, it needs consistent investment from governments, universities and research bodies to move forward," Lin said.
"Hong Kong can serve as a regional hub for quantum collaboration in the Asia-Pacific, connecting talent and capital from across the globe. Partners can co-develop prototypes first, before testing suitable routes for local adoption and wider regional scaling."
She noted that open quantum cloud platforms and Asia-Pacific joint research laboratories offer a viable model for collaboration.
Rather than one-off technology transfers, these initiatives focus on shared computing resources, joint experiments and cross-border academic exchanges.
In her view, inclusive access to technology cannot be achieved overnight and requires voluntary, long-term collaboration among economies at different stages of digital development.
Professor Wen Yonggang, Associate Provost of Nanyang Technological University and Fellow of the Singapore Academy of Engineering. 
Sustainable computing is another shared regional challenge.
Surging AI workloads are driving up data center power consumption, creating particular pressure on land-scarce economies in Southeast Asia.
Wen's research examines space-based data center designs. He says space-hosted computing could harness greater solar irradiance and natural radiative cooling in space, while orbital resources could help ease land constraints on Earth.
"Many Southeast Asian economies have expanded their data center footprint rapidly. Some are drawing lessons from Singapore's regulatory framework: aligning data center growth with renewable power supply, rolling out regular energy efficiency audits and putting guardrails in place to pursue greener digital infrastructure," Wen noted.
He believes innovators in the Asia-Pacific may carve out distinct technical pathways for next-generation computing, similar to the divergent development trajectories seen in the global electric vehicle sector.
Both experts observed that the digital divide across APEC economies means that uniform, top-down technology rollouts do not suit regional conditions.
For regional cooperation on frontier technologies for the public good, voluntary knowledge exchange, joint laboratory research and capacity building are more practical approaches.
They said regional stakeholders aim to translate advances in AI, quantum simulation and sustainable computing into tangible outcomes: stronger climate resilience, more accessible healthcare and improved social services.

A television station broadcasts Anthropic IPO news on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange in New York, US, October 26, 2026. 
US artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic publicly filed its prospectus for an initial public offering (IPO) on Monday, which could become the largest stock market debut in history.
The filing, a registration statement on Form S-1 with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, did not set the number of shares to be sold or a price range. Anthropic intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT, according to a release on the company's website.
Both the company and existing shareholders will sell shares, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley named first among 24 underwriters. The company is expected to begin trading in mid-November, and backers hope for a valuation of up to $2 trillion, though some investors have weighed a figure closer to $1.5 trillion, according to Reuters.
A news ticker displays Anthropic IPO news on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange in New York, US, October 26, 2026. 
The prospectus offers the first detailed look at the finances of the developer of the Claude AI models. Revenues reached $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $1.16 billion year on year, after growing from $41 million in 2023 to $386 million in 2024 and $4.59 billion in 2025. Revenues in the second quarter alone were $11.56 billion, and the company reported its first quarterly operating profit of $974 million.
The headline losses are far larger, but most stem from accounting charges rather than cash spending. Anthropic recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, of which $72.4 billion came from changes in the fair value of convertible notes and other instruments as the company's own valuation climbed. Its operating loss for the period was $693 million, while operating cash flow turned positive at $3.93 billion. Cash and short-term investments totaled $131.7 billion at June 30.
The filing warns that this rapid pace may not last. "We cannot assure you [revenue] will continue to grow at all," the company said in the prospectus, which also notes it is on track for a second consecutive quarter of adjusted operating profit.
Spending on computing power remains the central cost. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing resources and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, and has committed to $518 billion in future infrastructure spending. It has agreed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon through April 2036 and at least $114.5 billion with Google through July 2033. Amazon holds $6.2 billion of notes that convert into non-voting stock, capped at 12% of the company.
By September 30, more than 1,900 customers generated at least $1 million each in trailing annual revenue, and more than 11,900 generated at least $100,000, up from 950 a year earlier. Existing customers spend roughly nine times what they did a year ago, but two unnamed customers accounted for about 23% of revenues in the first half of 2026.
Public investors will be able to buy the shares but will not steer the company. A single Class F share held by the seven co-founders carries 50.1% of every stockholder vote, and a trust will elect a majority of the board. A Public Benefit Fund will hold 5% of the company in non-voting shares, and each co-founder has pledged to give 80% of their personal Anthropic equity to philanthropic causes.
The prospectus devotes sections to risk factors, including warnings that advanced AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" and that liability from extreme harm could exceed what any insurer can cover.
Anthropic raised $65 billion in May at a $965-billion valuation. A debut above $2 trillion would surpass SpaceX's $1.77-trillion listing in June, the current record. Reuters has reported Anthropic's third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion and forward projections pointing to revenue of about $190 billion to $200 billion in 2028.
